clue.text: Book about Russian ready to be awkward

indicators.note: the book's word wraps round the money, so 'about' says one piece encloses the other

parts.note: a tome is a large book
'ready' is slang for cash, and Russia's currency is the rouble

explanation.surface: A book about a Russian who is ready to be difficult.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Ready' is British slang for money ('ready cash'), not a state of preparedness.
explanation.definitionFit: Synonym: something awkward causes difficulty and bother.

clue.text: Stations for period in India

parts.note: a term is a period of time, as at school
I is India in the NATO phonetic alphabet

explanation.surface: Railway stations serving a period of service in India.
explanation.definitionFit: Plural synonym: end-of-line railway stations are called terminuses or termini.

clue.text: Public spell of cricket takes time

parts.note: an over is a set of six balls bowled in cricket

explanation.surface: A public spell of cricket match play that takes a while.
explanation.walkthrough: In cricket an OVER is a spell of six deliveries from one bowler.
explanation.definitionFit: Synonym: something done openly, in plain view, is public.

clue.text: Black Country man, I'm brought up in fog

indicators.note: the turned pair of letters sits within the word for fog

parts.note: brume is a literary word for mist or fog

indicators.note: in a down clue, brought up means read from bottom to top, so the letters run backwards

parts.note: taken as its letters, I and M

explanation.surface: A Midlands man says he was raised in fog.
explanation.walkthrough: A Brummie is someone from Birmingham; the setter loosely lumps the city in with the neighbouring industrial Black Country of the West Midlands.
explanation.definitionFit: Loose example: a native of Birmingham, next to England's industrial Black Country, gets this nickname.

clue.text: Lands in eastern parts of USA

parts.note: E is the abbreviation for east or eastern
the USA is made up of fifty states

explanation.surface: Lands located in the eastern parts of America.
explanation.definitionFit: Synonym: large landed properties owned by one person are lands.

clue.text: Present politician money from church

parts.note: to present something is to offer it
a Tory is a British Conservative politician

explanation.surface: A politician hands over cash taken from a church.
explanation.definitionFit: Description: the collection taken from the congregation during a church service has this name.

clue.text: Fancy gentle rambles around area?

indicators.note: the jumbled letters go round the short abbreviation
the word gentle wanders about, so its letters are jumbled

explanation.surface: A smart, gentle walk around some district, perhaps.
explanation.definitionFit: Synonym: as an adjective, fancy means stylish or refined.

clue.text: Upstart hit back with place being unfinished

indicators.note: hit back is read as the word for hit going backwards

parts.note: a rap is a sharp blow

indicators.note: the word for place loses its final letter

parts.note: a venue is a place where something happens

explanation.surface: A cheeky upstart retaliates against a half-built location.
explanation.definitionFit: Synonym: someone newly risen to wealth or status, regarded as not belonging, is an upstart.

clue.text: Investigates squalid hotels as place to hide out

parts.note: to pry is to investigate nosily

indicators.note: the hotels are in a messy state, so their letters are scrambled

explanation.surface: A detective checks grubby hotels as a hideout.
explanation.walkthrough: A priest's hole was a hiding place built in English houses for Catholic priests during their persecution.
explanation.definitionFit: Description: secret chambers concealed persecuted Catholic clergy in Tudor and Stuart houses.

clue.text: Cheese after a major component of it's turned to silky stuff

indicators.note: the cheese comes after the turned ingredient
the word for that ingredient is turned round and read backwards

parts.note: cheese contains a lot of fat; 'it' is the cheese
feta is a Greek cheese

explanation.surface: Cheese that a major component of it has turned into something silky.
explanation.walkthrough: 'It' refers back to cheese, whose major component is fat; the 's is 'is'.
explanation.definitionFit: Description: a crisp, lustrous silk fabric goes by this name.

clue.text: I see batsmen playing skiving off work

indicators.note: the batsmen at play throw the letters into a new order

explanation.surface: Watching cricketers bat instead of being at the office.
explanation.definitionFit: Synonym: habitually staying away from your job without reason.

clue.text: Charlie's just the thing to snare fashion designer endlessly

definitions.note: Charlie is, i.e. a Charlie, British slang for a fool

indicators.note: the phrase for the right thing catches the designer inside it

parts.note: 'it' means exactly what is wanted

indicators.note: the designer's name loses its last letter

parts.note: Christian Dior was a French fashion designer

explanation.surface: Charlie is the perfect bait to trap a fashion designer.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Charlie' is British slang for a fool.
explanation.definitionFit: Synonym: a Charlie in British slang is a fool or dimwit.

clue.text: Friend with top off tests fabrics

parts.note: a mate is a friend

indicators.note: the word for tests loses its first letter

parts.note: trials are tests

explanation.surface: A friend tries on fabrics without a top.
explanation.definitionFit: Synonym: cloths and textiles are fabrics.

clue.text: Nieces excited about first bit of chemical knowledge

indicators.note: the scrambled letters go round the single letter
the nieces are agitated, so their letters are scrambled
take only the opening letter of chemical

explanation.surface: Nieces are thrilled by a little chemistry lesson.
explanation.definitionFit: Synonym: systematic understanding of the world is knowledge.

clue.text: Now eat top cooked vegetable

indicators.note: the words are cooked up, so their letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: Dig in now to the best cooked vegetable.
explanation.definitionFit: Example: an early-season potato is a kind of vegetable.

clue.text: Cut around edges of tile to make smaller

indicators.note: the word for cut goes round the picked letters

parts.note: shorn means cut, as hair or wool

indicators.note: take the first and last letters of tile

explanation.surface: Trim round the borders of a tile so it fits.
explanation.definitionFit: Synonym: to reduce the length of something is to make it smaller.

clue.text: Bad hands move slowly on board steamship

indicators.note: being on board the ship means sitting inside its abbreviation

parts.note: to crawl is to move slowly

explanation.surface: Poor crew members dawdle aboard a steamer.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Hands' looks like crew, but here it means handwriting.
explanation.definitionFit: Synonym: untidy handwriting is a bad hand, and messy scribbles are bad hands.

clue.text: Boring brief relationship after scripture lesson

indicators.note: the relationship comes after the school subject

parts.note: RI is religious instruction, the old school subject
a fling is a short affair

explanation.surface: A dull short romance following a religion class.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Boring' is not dull here: it is cutting spiral grooves inside a gun barrel.
explanation.definitionFit: Technical sense: cutting grooves into a gun barrel is boring it out.

clue.text: Terrible investor runs out broke?

indicators.note: a terrible investor is a mess, so the letters are rearranged

parts.note: R is the cricket abbreviation for runs

explanation.surface: A dreadful investor's money runs out and he ends up broke.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Runs out' says take R (cricket's runs) away from the fodder before rearranging what is left.
explanation.definitionFit: Idiom: something stove in has been smashed inwards, so broke in the sense of broken.

clue.text: Stick around liking hot stuff

indicators.note: the stick goes round the word for liking

parts.note: a cane is a walking stick
a yen is a longing or liking

explanation.surface: Carrying a stick around while fancying spicy food.
explanation.definitionFit: Example: this fiery red chilli powder is hot stuff.

clue.text: Clergymen showing posh style in old cars

indicators.note: the letter for posh sits inside the old cars

parts.note: a crate is slang for an old, battered car
U means upper-class, as in 'U and non-U' usage

explanation.surface: Clergymen showing off upper-class style in vintage cars.
explanation.definitionFit: Example: assistant parish priests in the Church of England are clergymen.

clue.text: Nervy about head of tribunal being unbiased

indicators.note: the nerve word goes round the picked letter

parts.note: neural means relating to the nerves

indicators.note: take the first letter of tribunal

explanation.surface: A jittery tribunal chairman tries to stay impartial.
explanation.definitionFit: Synonym: taking no side is being impartial.

clue.text: Sick of commander interrupting meal

parts.note: taken as written

indicators.note: the commander breaks into the word for meal

parts.note: meal is ground grain, i.e. flour
CO is the abbreviation for commanding officer

explanation.surface: Sickened by an officer barging in on dinner.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Meal' looks like dinner, but it is ground grain.
explanation.definitionFit: Idiom: feeling slightly unwell or below par is being sick.

clue.text: Time accompanied by one alluring woman

parts.note: an hour is a unit of time
I is the Roman numeral one

explanation.surface: A man spends time accompanied by a seductive woman.
explanation.definitionFit: Mythology: a beautiful nymph of the Islamic paradise, so a voluptuous, alluring woman.

clue.text: Pivotal point of fishing expedition

indicators.note: the answer is made of letters lying inside the words that follow

explanation.surface: The crucial moment of an angling trip.
explanation.definitionFit: Description: the joint on which a door swings is its pivotal point.

clue.text: Have a close shave as English exercise cut short

indicators.note: the exercise loses its final letter

parts.note: Pilates is a system of body-conditioning exercise

explanation.surface: An Englishman's workout is curtailed after a narrow escape.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Have a close shave' suggests a near miss, but it means remove hair.
explanation.definitionFit: Literal reading: removing body hair at the root is a very close shave.

clue.text: Non-drinker swallowing an alcoholic drink in fit of temper

indicators.note: the teetotaller gulps down the little word, which goes inside

parts.note: TT stands for teetotal
rum is a spirit

explanation.surface: A teetotaller downs a stiff drink and throws a fit.
explanation.definitionFit: Synonym: an angry outburst, especially a child's, is a fit of temper.

clue.text: Increase in support gives good basic training

definitions.meaning: a growing tide of public backing
read as two words, a teacher who grounds pupils well

explanation.surface: Popularity rises because the course offers solid instruction.
explanation.definitionFit: Idiom: a surge of popular feeling is an increase in support, from the ocean swell.
